headline: City auditor reports FY26 general fund ended with $10 million deficit, drawn from reserves.
summary: The auditor said revenues came in about $1 million short, and a $3 million snow and ice deficit was offset by about $1 million in department turnbacks. The water fund had net income of $1.5 million, and the sewer fund had $2.4 million. Without a transfer from the general stabilization fund, the parking fund would have lost $1.3 million. The subcommittee plans to work with the administration on the fiscal year '28 budget early in the new year.
discussion: Wage ordinance history: Members raised concern about large raises at the top of the pay scale, citing one position that went from $181,000 to $251,000. Human resources said the city is in a decent spot but must pay enough to keep staff.
General fund reserves: The auditor said reserves were used to balance the budget for a second year in a row. The auditor said this could point to a structural deficit that might need to be addressed.

Tax levy collections: The auditor said $186 million of the $188 million tax levy was collected, and the other $2 million will be collected in future years. A member asked whether the gap came from unpaid bills or from estimating errors.

Parking enterprise fund: The auditor said the fund lost $1.3 million without the stabilization transfer, due to higher contractor costs and garage repairs. Members asked whether card fees are passed on to drivers, and the auditor said everyone pays the same rate.
Indirect costs: Members asked how indirect charges to enterprise funds are set. The auditor said the CFO's office calculates them, covering administrative costs, health insurance, and retirement.
